tradition.name: Japanese Buddhist chant
tradition.lineage: Japanese Buddhist chant encompasses the vocal practices of Japan’s Buddhist schools and lay communities. Transmitted from continental Asia and developed through distinct temple lineages, it ranges from elaborate shōmyō to syllabic sutra recitation, ceremonial narratives and devotional hymns. Clergy and lay practitioners preserve these traditions through ritual, instruction and communal singing.

extras.description: Voices carry sacred texts through sustained melodic phrases or measured syllabic recitation. Some rituals use bells, bowls, gongs and cymbals as signals, while vocal passages place the sound and meaning of the text at the centre of the practice.
exemplars: Shōmyō, sutra recitation, kōshiki and goeika traditions

tradition.name: Vintage Italian Soundtrack
tradition.lineage: Vintage Italian soundtrack music draws on the film and studio archives of the 1960s–80s, where jazz, orchestral writing, pop, funk and psychedelic textures served comedy, crime, horror and other screen genres. Reissue and licensing communities around CAM Sugar and Sonor Music Editions have renewed circulation of this repertoire. Alongside orchestral scores, studio groups such as I Marc 4 supplied compact, groove-led themes built from guitar, organ, bass and drums.

extras.description: Short thematic cues move between memorable melody, rhythmic accompaniment and contrasting instrumental colours. Electric organ, guitar and a bass-and-drum rhythm section support the jazz-funk studio-combo strand, while the wider archival field also includes orchestral, electronic and vocal film music.

tradition.name: Samba Moderno
tradition.lineage: Samba moderno follows the contemporary Rio singer-composer network nurtured by Lapa venues, Clube Renascença, Cacique de Ramos and projects such as Samba Social Clube and Festa da Raça. Artists including João Martins, Inácio Rios and Nego Álvaro carry older samba traditions into new compositions, collaborations and independent careers.

extras.description: Melodic singing and shared refrains interlock with compact cavaquinho or banjo accompaniment, guitar and layered hand percussion. New songs about affection, everyday life and social experience circulate between neighborhood rodas, studio releases and concert stages, retaining the rhythmic conversation of samba while developing individual poetic voices.
